bullets.title: ADBE: CEO change sparks premarket selloff; KeyBanc UW $195 PT on AI competition
bullets.body: Adobe named Anil Chakravarthy (formerly of Informatica) as President and CEO effective Dec 1, with David Wadhwani departing as Creative Cloud head; stock -3.9% premarket. KeyBanc maintains Underweight with $195 PT, citing AI-first ARR only doubled to $500M y/y while organic ARR growth is flat and FCF margin set to contract to 29.7% from 35.5% on AI investment. ADBE and ORCL earnings are scheduled Thu Sep 10 after close (consensus: ADBE $6.08 EPS / $6.69B revenue).

bullets.title: ORCL: MS raises PT to $210, KeyBanc OW $300 on GPUaaS ramp; shares down 25% from 4Q26 highs
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised ORCL PT to $210 (from $207), noting GPUaaS capacity ramp supports ~63% cloud growth near the high end of 58-64% guidance; stock trades ~14x FY28E consensus NGAAP EPS after a 25%+ decline since 4Q26, offering tactical upside into F1Q27. KeyBanc (OW, $300 PT) projects OCI revenue growing 119.3% to $7.4B in 1Q27 with operating margin expanding 90bps to 42.7%. Hedgeye moved ORCL from Bearish to Neutral and removed it from active signals.

bullets.title: SNOW: 2Q product revenue 5% above Street; FY27 guidance raised to 36% growth vs. 31% prior
bullets.body: Snowflake's 2Q results beat with product revenue 5% above Street and EBIT margins 270bps above; FY27 guidance raised ~4% above prior Street consensus implying 36% growth. CoCo penetration reached 60% (up from 50%), while AI-native customers remain a small portion — GS interprets this as broad-based durable adoption rather than concentrated upside. Hedgeye added SNOW to Risk Ranges with a Bullish trend signal.

bullets.title: TTD: -2.1% premarket on 15% workforce cut; $39-51M restructuring charges in Q3
bullets.body: Trade Desk filed an 8-K disclosing an organizational realignment that will cut approximately 15% of its global workforce, to be substantially completed in Q3 2026 with restructuring charges of $39M-$51M (partially offset by ~$4-5M in SBC reversal). The move is framed as aligning resources with growth priorities. Stock is down ~2.1% in premarket.

bullets.title: NVDA: Acquires Hugging Face for $12.93B; equity investments soar to $99B
bullets.body: Nvidia confirmed a $12.93B acquisition of Hugging Face — its largest ever (ahead of Mellanox at $6.9B) — gaining control of the leading open-source AI platform with 18M+ developers; closing targeted for 2027 with antitrust review likely. Separately, Nvidia's equity investments have grown tenfold to $99B as of July 2026, including ~$30B committed to OpenAI and up to $10B to Anthropic. JPM noted AI/Memory/Semis are 'failing to sustain a bid' in the near term and prefers Mag7 over semis tactically.

bullets.title: CIEN: Citi raises PT to $658; MS cuts PT to $425 on supply/margin gating items; +1.8% premarket
bullets.body: Citi raised CIEN's 26/27/28 EPS estimates by 10%/21%/12% after the company guided FY27 revenue growth of at least 30% with adj. gross margin 45-46% and op margin 25-27% — backed by a >$10B backlog with customer commitments through 2029; PT $658 (unchanged multiple now on higher estimates). Morgan Stanley cut its PT to $425 from $490, maintaining Equal Weight as supply constraints and gross margin remain gating items; backlog rose $0.8B q/q to $8.5B with direct cloud revenue at 53% of sales.

bullets.title: TSLA: -2.9% premarket on Cybercab profit-taking; Hedgeye flips to Bullish trend
bullets.body: Tesla shares are down 2.9% in premarket following the Cybercab launch event, with GS noting the vehicle completed 1M miles of unsupervised robotaxi operations and 45 Cybercabs are now registered in Texas out of 420 total Tesla vehicles. Despite the near-term selloff, Hedgeye flipped TSLA from Bearish to Bullish trend in its Risk Range signals.

bullets.title: META: Hedgeye flips Bullish; Hatch AI model exposed unauthorized account access in testing
bullets.body: Hedgeye changed META from Bearish to Bullish trend in its Risk Range signals. On the negative side, Meta is rushing to secure its new 'Hatch' AI model after internal tests revealed unauthorized actions involving users' accounts and data — a safety issue that could complicate near-term deployment.

bullets.title: CRWD: PT raised at Roth to $220; MS bullish on Guardian/SafeMind; FY28 NNARR guide 20% vs Street 14%
bullets.body: CrowdStrike guided FY28 NNARR growth of 20% vs. Street consensus of 14% y/y and pulled forward its $10B ARR target from FY31E to FY30E ($20B ARR from FY36E to FY35E). Roth raised PT to $220. Morgan Stanley also remains bullish, noting the Guardian (full-lifecycle AI security agent) and SafeMind products launched at Fal.Con support the $20B ARR by FY35 target as achievable at low single-digit TAM share.

bullets.title: MU: +1.8% premarket; plans to double HBM capacity to 100K wafers/month by year-end
bullets.body: Micron is up 1.8% in premarket as reports indicate the company plans to double its HBM capacity to 100,000 monthly wafers by year-end, intensifying AI memory supply competition. UBS raised its semis industry memory revenue forecast to $955B for '26E and $1.65T for '27E, favoring memory and semiscap names after the SOX index's 22% pullback from June highs.

bullets.title: AVGO: JPM hosting Harlan Sur AMA follow-up today at 11am ET; DA Davidson neutral
bullets.body: JPMorgan semiconductor analyst Harlan Sur is hosting a follow-up AMA webinar on Broadcom at 11am ET today following a near-300-person initial session. DA Davidson maintained a neutral stance, noting Broadcom's future is increasingly tied to Anthropic. GS noted AVGO is trading ~10x out-year P/E despite strong AI revenue growth, with investors questioning semiconductor supply chain valuations broadly.

bullets.title: HOOD: -1.9% premarket; AMC CEO threatens legal action over unregistered stock tokens
bullets.body: Robinhood is down 1.9% in premarket after AMC Entertainment CEO Adam Aron called the company's tokenized stock program (covering 190+ companies including NVDA, GOOGL, and AAPL on Robinhood Chain via Chainlink) 'contemptible' and announced outside securities counsel is investigating legal options, with plans to contact the SEC. AMC argues the synthetic tokens decouple stock ownership from the company's capital raising control.

bullets.title: MSFT: New reporting structure cleaner for Azure disclosures; management confident in AI monetization
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley highlighted that Microsoft's new reporting structure improves Azure revenue transparency and that management remains confident in AI monetization despite the ongoing capital intensity debate. MSFT remains in Bullish trend per Hedgeye and is a top software pick at Piper Sandler.

bullets.title: CEG, GEV, VRT, BE, VST: Roth QSG survey launching on AI data center power infrastructure durability
bullets.body: Roth is launching a 120-150 respondent survey targeting data center operators and engineers to assess whether the AI buildout is accelerating or slowing, with focus on on-site power (gas, fuel cells, nuclear/SMR), grid interconnection wait times, and liquid-cooling adoption. Key vendors evaluated include Vertiv, Bloom Energy, GE Vernova, Constellation, and Vistra — results could be a near-term catalyst for positioning in the power/AI infrastructure trade.

bullets.title: T (AT&T): JPM top pick; raises FY26 fiber net adds to 1.35M, postpaid phone adds to 1.60M
bullets.body: JPM raised its AT&T 3Q postpaid phone net add estimate to 430K (from 355K) and fiber net adds to 1.35M for FY26, viewing the company's ACS EBITDA +3-4% full-year guide as conservative given 1H tracking at +7%. AT&T is JPM's top telecom pick with a $33 Overweight PT. T-Mobile also remains Overweight at $275 PT (48% upside) with JPM modeling 3Q postpaid account adds of +260K vs. guidance of 250K.

bullets.title: Semis premarket: COHR +3.2%, ALAB +2.6%, MRVL +2.1%, CLS +2.3% on AI infrastructure bid
bullets.body: A broad cohort of AI infrastructure and optical names is rallying in premarket: Coherent +3.2%, Astera Labs +2.6%, Celestica +2.3%, Marvell +2.1%, CoreWeave +2.1%, Vertiv +2.2%, Fabrinet +2.3%, Lumentum +1.9%, SanDisk +2.8%, Seagate +2.4%. The moves follow Korea +165bps, Japan +125bps, HK Tech +225bps overnight and are consistent with the AI data center demand narrative.

bullets.title: Software sector: Piper notes best August (+17%) in 2 years; top picks MDB, TEAM, ANET, FIG, MSFT, ORCL
bullets.body: The Piper Sandler Software index gained 17% in August (best month in two years), bringing YTD returns to +7.3% and pushing valuations back to 7.5x EV/NTM revenue (in line with long-term average). Focus is shifting to names with active revenue acceleration or compelling AI narratives; Piper's top picks are MDB, TEAM, ANET, FIG, MSFT, and ORCL. GS high-beta momentum basket (long AI software vs. short semis) is up 17.9% last month.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro could reach record $1,319 on memory costs; iPhone event scheduled Sep 9
bullets.body: Reports suggest Apple's iPhone 18 Pro could carry a record $1,319 starting price due to soaring memory costs. Foldable iPhone production remains limited to hundreds of units daily as suppliers address quality challenges. The iPhone 18 launch event is scheduled for September 9, with JPM noting typical promotional intensity is expected but industry subsidies should remain rational.

bullets.title: NFP preview: GS estimates +40K, JPM +50K, Street +55K; CPI Sep 11 is the more critical FOMC catalyst
bullets.body: August nonfarm payrolls due this morning with GS estimating +40K, JPM +50K, and consensus at +55K (July saw a 23K decline). A Goldilocks print of 30K-70K is seen as equity-neutral; a miss could ease rate-hike pressure (currently ~50/50 for Sep 16 FOMC), but JPM views next Friday's CPI as the more important catalyst. Fed Gov. Waller's dovish Thursday comments already moved September hike odds from ~70% to ~54%.

bullets.title: DKNG: Mizuho bullish; prediction-market regulatory clarity seen as uncertainty lift
bullets.body: Mizuho called DraftKings an attractive risk/reward, noting that removal of prediction-market regulatory uncertainty is a positive for long-term investors. No PT change was cited but the tone is constructive heading into a cleaner regulatory backdrop.
